steps.title: Import Angular core modules and components
steps.instruction: Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbols you need from their respective Angular packages.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'
// Import CommonModule from '@angular/common'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular core modules are imported to set up a component-based architecture.
successCriteria: Component and OnInit are imported from '@angular/core', and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core Angular modules needed for component development.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing all three required symbols: Component, OnInit, and CommonModule from their correct packages.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Create main AppComponent with TypeScript class
steps.instruction: Define the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator and implement the OnInit interface.
steps.hint: Use the class keyword to define AppComponent, add @Component decorator above it with a selector and template, and implement OnInit.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with proper Angular component structure and TypeScript interface implementation.
successCriteria:
AppComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-root', template '

App works!

', and implements OnInit with ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main AppComponent with proper Angular component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your AppComponent has the @Component decorator with selector and template, and implements OnInit.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined the AppComponent class with @Component decorator and implemented OnInit interface.

steps.title: Add component metadata with template and styles
steps.instruction: Add the selector, templateUrl, and styleUrls properties to the @Component decorator of your AppComponent. Use 'app-root' for selector, './app.component.html' for templateUrl, and ['./app.component.css'] for styleUrls.
steps.hint: The @Component decorator should include these three properties. Make sure styleUrls is an array with the CSS file path.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have its metadata configured for rendering with a template and styles.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes selector: 'app-root', templateUrl: './app.component.html', and styleUrls: ['./app.component.css'].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've configured the component metadata correctly. This tells Angular how to render and style your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some metadata, but check that all three properties (selector, templateUrl, styleUrls) are present with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component metadata is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add selector, templateUrl, and styleUrls properties to the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Initialize component state with server-side rendering flag
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, create a property called isServerRendered and set its initial value to true.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration with type annotation in the class body, like 'propertyName: type = initialValue'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state property that tracks whether it was rendered on the server, which is important for understanding SSR concepts.
successCriteria: The AppComponent class contains a property named isServerRendered with type boolean and initial value true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the server-side rendering state property. This flag will help demonstrate SSR behavior in Angular.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the property is named exactly 'isServerRendered' with type boolean and initial value true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The property wasn't added correctly. Remember to create a property called 'isServerRendered' with type boolean and set it to true inside the AppComponent class.

steps.title: Add ngOnInit lifecycle hook
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add the ngOnInit() method to demonstrate component initialization for server-side rendering awareness.
steps.hint: Implement the ngOnInit method from the OnInit interface you already imported.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class now has a properly implemented ngOnInit lifecycle method.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method is defined with a void return type and empty body in the AppComponent class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the ngOnInit lifecycle hook. This method will execute when the component initializes, which is important for understanding when server-side rendering occurs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the ngOnInit method with the correct syntax and placed it inside the AppComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method is missing or has incorrect syntax. Remember to implement it as part of the AppComponent class that implements the OnInit interface.

steps.title: Create template structure with header section
steps.instruction: In the component's metadata, add a template property with a header element containing a title explaining server-side rendering concepts.
steps.hint: Add a template property to the @Component decorator with a string containing an HTML header element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic template structure with a header section that introduces server-side rendering concepts.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a template property with a header element containing a title about server-side rendering.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the template structure with a header section. This provides the foundation for displaying content about server-side rendering.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a template, but make sure it includes a header element with a title about server-side rendering concepts.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure wasn't properly added. Check that you added a template property to the @Component decorator with a header element containing a title.

steps.title: Display server-side rendering status in template
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a paragraph element that displays the current value of the isServerRendered property using Angular interpolation syntax.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the property value inside the paragraph text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a boolean state in template

Server-side rendering enabled: {{ isServerRendered }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show a paragraph that dynamically displays whether server-side rendering is enabled based on the component's state.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that uses interpolation to display the isServerRendered property value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph that displays the server-side rendering status using interpolation. This demonstrates how Angular templates can dynamically show component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct interpolation syntax with double curly braces {{ }} around the property name.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph with interpolation for isServerRendered wasn't found. Remember to add a

element in the template that uses {{ isServerRendered }} to display the property value.

steps.title: Add static generation explanation section
steps.instruction: In the component template, add a <div> element with a class of 'section' and a heading that explains static site generation principles.
steps.hint: Add the new <div> after the existing header section in your template. Include an <h2> heading with descriptive text about SSG.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a static content section in Angular template

Static Site Generation (SSG)

Content explaining SSG principles...
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have a new section with a heading explaining static site generation concepts.
successCriteria: A <div> element with class 'section' containing an <h2> heading about SSG principles is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a static content section to demonstrate SSG concepts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added content, but make sure it's a <div> with class 'section' and includes an <h2> heading about SSG principles.
steps.feedbackWrong: The static generation explanation section wasn't added correctly. Please add a <div> with class 'section' containing an <h2> heading about SSG.

steps.title: Create comparison table structure
steps.instruction: Add a table element with headers for SSR and SSG comparison points inside the template.
steps.hint: Use the <table> HTML element with <thead> and <tr> for the header row, and <th> for column headers.
steps.expectedOutcome: A table element with headers for SSR and SSG comparison points is added to the template.
successCriteria: The template contains a <table> element with <thead>, <tr>, and <th> elements for SSR and SSG headers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the table structure for comparing SSR and SSG.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included all required table elements: <table>, <thead>, <tr>, and <th> for SSR and SSG headers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table structure is missing or incomplete. Please add a <table> element with headers for SSR and SSG comparison points.

steps.title: Populate comparison table with data
steps.instruction: Inside the template, replace the comment '<!-- Add comparison table here -->' with a table that compares SSR and SSG characteristics. Include rows for performance, SEO, and use cases with appropriate data.
steps.hint: Use HTML table tags (<table>, <thead>, <tbody>, <tr>, <th>, <td>) to create the table structure. Fill each cell with relevant comparison data.
steps.analogousExample:
Characteristic SSR SSG
Performance Dynamic per request Pre-built static
steps.expectedOutcome: A comparison table appears in the component template showing differences between SSR and SSG across multiple characteristics.
successCriteria: The template contains a complete HTML table with headers and at least three data rows comparing SSR and SSG characteristics.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a comparison table that clearly illustrates the differences between SSR and SSG rendering strategies.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the table, but it needs more complete data. Make sure to include rows for performance, SEO, and use cases with appropriate comparison data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The comparison table is missing or incomplete. Check that you've replaced the comment with a proper HTML table structure containing comparison data.
